notes: PATHWAY-only scoring (models are single-label pathway NER; DISEASE spans were removed from gt_100). Two metrics reported side by side; partial never replaces exact. seqeval = entity-level F1/P/R (train.py convention, used for models). exact_span = exact character-offset set match (used for span sources). partial = gold-coverage F1/P/R at threshold 0.5: a predicted span counts when it covers >=50% of the gold span's characters, greedy one-to-one. Scripts: scripts/score_gt_100.py, scripts/compare_vs_gt100.py

basis.rule: All 100 gt_100 PMIDs are scored. A PMID with no prediction counts as zero predictions rather than being dropped.
basis.gt_100_in_pathway_10k: all 100 PMIDs are present in data/processed/pathway-10k/{articles.jsonl,splits.json} (10125 PMIDs each) and all 100 fall in the *test* split, cross-confirmed by meta.split=='test' on every gt_100 record — so the runs-truba-checkpoints/pathway-10k/* models never trained on them
basis.matches_jsonl_caveat: data/processed/pathway-10k/matches.jsonl holds only PMIDs with at least one pathway hit (9168 of 10125); intersecting on it would drop exactly the recall failures, which is why the earlier 91-PMID basis was replaced

superseded_91_pmid_basis.note: earlier figure, scored only on the 91 PMIDs present in matches.jsonl; kept for traceability

span_sources.pipeline: local Ollama qwen2.5:14b pathway extraction; spans carry source=llm_silver. data/doccano/pathway_remaining_6125_doccano.jsonl is the doccano rendering of the same output (span sets identical on all 100 PMIDs).
span_sources.observation: Precision is respectable but recall is the bottleneck: 223 predicted spans against 279 gold, and 76 gold spans have zero overlapping LLM span. The misses are systematically free-text pathway mentions outside the query vocabulary ('production of reactive oxygen species', 'AA cascade', 'DNPS pathway', 'energy metabolism'). By match_type the produced spans are near-perfect (exact 69/70, synonym 7/7, variation 25/26 land on gold); only unmapped lags at 92/120. The silver therefore scores below the NER models trained from it.

span_sources.pipeline: llm/run_silver.py with --model <checkpoint> (llm/annotators.py NERAnnotator: 512-token windows, stride 64, word-level offsets), --articles doccano/golden_dataset/gt_100.jsonl --text-field text --matches none --all --allow-golden
span_sources.source: NER checkpoint via run_silver, booster on

span_sources.pipeline: llm/run_silver.py with --model <checkpoint> (llm/annotators.py NERAnnotator: 512-token windows, stride 64, word-level offsets), --articles doccano/golden_dataset/gt_100.jsonl --text-field text --matches none --all --allow-golden
span_sources.source: NER checkpoint via run_silver, booster off
span_sources.observation: The booster (llm/booster.py) adds exactly one span over these 100 abstracts and it is a true positive: exact F1 0.8364 -> 0.8386. It was built to patch LLM recall gaps and has almost nothing left to add on top of a NER checkpoint, which already finds the Recon vocabulary itself. Keeping it on is free and costs no precision here; it is not what makes this source strong. Scored with scripts/compare_vs_gt100.py, so these are character-offset set matches, comparable to the other span_sources rows and NOT to the seqeval numbers under `models` — though for this checkpoint they agree to 0.002, which is itself evidence the word-level offset decoding is right.
